an9.12:3.1: “This morning, sir, I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
an9.12:3.3: “It’s too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī;
an9.12:3.4: why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?”
an9.12:3.5: So I went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.
an9.12:3.6: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, I sat down to one side.
an9.12:3.7: Now at that time while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together this discussion came up among them:
an9.12:3.8: “Reverends, no one who dies with residue is exempt from hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm. They’re not exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.”
an9.12:3.9: Sir, I neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions.
an9.12:3.10: Neither approving nor rejecting it, I rose from my seat and left, thinking:
an9.12:3.11: “‘I will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.’”
